_comment: WATCHDOG session MCP config. The watchdog server ONLY.
motion, gripper and scene are absent by design, and this is the core
architectural rule of the whole setup: a watchdog that can command the arm
is a second controller, not an independent observer. The watchdog still sees
everything the executor does -- observation flows through the ROS event bus
wait_for_event), never through holding the executor's command tools.
MUST be launched with --strict-mcp-config. Without it, --mcp-config MERGES
with the project .mcp.json and this session silently regains motion, gripper
and scene (verified: 42 tools merged vs 1 with --strict). That merge is
invisible from inside the session unless you list tools.
WATCHDOG_SESSION_DIR is deliberately NOT set here -- see executor.mcp.json's
note. Both configs omit it so both roles resolve the same bringup-written
pointer; a value here would have to match the executor's byte-for-byte and

args: unset VIRTUAL_ENV && source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash && source ~/watchdog/WatchDog_V1/ros2_ws/install/setup.bash && ros2 run robot_backend watchdog_mcp_server

_venv_comment: unset VIRTUAL_ENV is load-bearing, not tidiness. These servers are launched with bash -lc, a LOGIN shell, which auto-activates agents/.venv. mcp_servers/__init__._find_preferred_venv_python() checks $VIRTUAL_ENV BEFORE walking to the workspace venv, so the login shell silently wins and the server re-execs into agents/.venv -- which carries mcp 2.1.1 (FastMCP removed, renamed MCPServer) and no trimesh. The server then dies on import and the session reports CONNECTION_CLOSED with no hint as to why. Unsetting it lets resolution fall through to ros2_ws/.venv (mcp 1.29.1 with FastMCP, trimesh 5.1.0), which is the interpreter these servers are built against. Verified 2026-09-22.
